t.E341.agn: In 2019 EFSA set a group acceptable daily intake (ADI) for phosphates of 40 mg/kg body weight, expressed as phosphorus. It reported that, together with phosphorus from all sources, average intake in infants, toddlers and children, and high intake in adolescents, may exceed this limit.
t.E341.body: Phosphate additives dissolve in the digestive tract and dissociate into free phosphate (orthophosphate); di-, tri- and polyphosphates are also converted to orthophosphate. About 80–90% of this phosphorus is absorbed; it is not converted into another substance in the body and is excreted in the urine via the kidneys.
t.E341.eff.0.t: Together with phosphorus from all sources, the daily limit may be exceeded
t.E341.eff.0.w: Infants, toddlers and children (average intake), adolescents (high intake)
t.E341.prod: Obtained chemically from phosphoric acid produced from phosphate rock.
t.E341.pw.0: According to EFSA, phosphate intake from all sources may exceed the daily limit in children.
t.E341.pw.1: According to EFSA, phosphate intake from all sources may exceed the daily limit in infants.
t.E341.regx.0: Re-evaluated; group ADI 40 mg/kg (as phosphorus); may be exceeded in children.
t.E341.summary: The calcium salts of phosphoric acid. Used as raising agents, anti-caking agents and a source of calcium.
t.E341.what: Regulates acidity; used in baking powders and to prevent caking. Phosphorus is a mineral the body needs and also occurs naturally in foods.
